chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, عليهم السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah, صلى الله عليه وآله, said:
Beware of debt, for it is a disgrace to religion.

key_terms.آبَائِهِمْ: his forefathers, referring to the chain through the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.الدَّيْنَ: debt; financial liability owed by a person
key_terms.الدِّينِ: religion; one's religious standing and practice
key_terms.السَّكُونِيُّ: Al-Sakuni, the narrator transmitting the hadith
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Why does the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله warn against debt?
ai.summary: This hadith warns believers against falling into debt and presents indebtedness as something that tarnishes one's religion. It emphasizes the moral and spiritual burden of debt, highlighting financial responsibility and caution in one's dealings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3680 - Al-Sakuni narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said:
"Beware of debt, for it is a disgrace to religion."
